html:
The Siuslaw are a Native American people of the central Oregon coast, along the Siuslaw River around today's Florence. They lived in plank-house villages and fished for salmon, gathered shellfish and hunted elk.

Their language, Siuslaw, was closely related to that of the Lower Umpqua to the south; both are now extinct. In 1855 they signed a coast treaty that the US Senate never ratified, and in the following years they were confined to the Coast Reservation, where many died. Today they are part of the Confederated Tribes of Coos, Lower Umpqua and Siuslaw Indians, together with their Hanis Coos neighbours, a tribe the US recognised again in 1984.
